caption:
Flood risk and pipeline theft in Nigeria share a structural trait: the geography of the problem does not match the geography of the response. A reservoir sits in one jurisdiction. The floodplain it can drown sits in another, often across a state or even a border. A pipeline right-of-way runs through multiple local government areas, each with its own security posture and none with visibility into the whole corridor.

This is why dam management reads as an upstream engineering decision but lands as a downstream emergency, and why pipeline theft persists despite dense ground patrols — the corridor is long, the incentive is a price margin, and no single command owns the full line of sight.

None of this is new. It is publicly documented in flood bulletins and pipeline-loss reporting every year. The pattern holds because the response is still organized by administrative boundary, not by basin or by corridor.
thread: Nigeria's flood and pipeline-theft problems share a structural flaw: the risk follows a river basin or a pipeline corridor. The response follows administrative boundaries. Those two maps rarely line up.
A dam release decision sits with one authority. The floodplain it can drown sits in another jurisdiction downstream — sometimes another state. That gap is where warning time gets lost.
A pipeline corridor crosses dozens of local government areas. Each has its own patrol posture. None has a single view of the whole line. Theft economics exploit exactly that seam.

Public flood bulletins and pipeline-loss reports document this every year. The pattern doesn't repeat because it's random. It repeats because the response is organized by map lines that don't match the risk.

card.headline: The risk follows a basin. The response follows a border
card.sub: Dam releases and pipeline corridors cross jurisdictions the security response does not. That mismatch, not chance, drives the annual pattern.

rationale: Introduces a distinct, publicly-grounded CONTEXT angle — jurisdictional mismatch between risk geography and administrative response — without repeating prior decision, cadence, or limits framings.
